title: Windowed Reservoir Admission + Graceful Fallbacks for Tenant Fairness
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: During multi-region spikes we observe noisy neighbors and long-tail latency from a small set of tenants consuming bursty throughput. Existing token-bucket and priority-lane shedding provide coarse protection but: 1) they are static and penalize tenants with transiently high writes; 2) they lack temporal smoothing across short windows which leads to oscillation when capacity recovers; 3) there is no programmable mapping from admission budget to graceful degradation modes (e.g., slim responses, cached fallbacks, model-variant routing).

Goal: Implement a Windowed Reservoir Admission Controller (WRAC) that: (a) tracks per-tenant reservoir capacity over sliding windows (configurable 30s/5m/1h), (b) enforces probabilistic admission when reservoirs are depleted, (c) maps admission outcomes to an ordered set of graceful fallbacks (response-slimming, coarse-model, cached-response, immediate-429), and (d) supports cross-region fast failover with preserved reservoir state where possible.

Why this is different: Instead of pure token buckets we use time-windowed reservoirs with decay and capacity borrowing rules that prioritize fairness for tenants with sustained low-to-moderate usage while limiting unlimited bursters. This reduces oscillation and aligns admission signals with SLO windows. The design ties admission decisions to explicit degradation modes so client-observable behavior is predictable and testable.

User-facing constraints: No change to API surface; behavior controlled by per-tenant config accessible to SRE/Customer Success (via Console). Default policy must be conservative: no more than 5% of requests from a paying tenant are downgraded to a lower-fidelity model in steady-state.

Non-goals: This ticket does not implement Console UI for editing policies (follow-up). It also does not add billing changes for degraded tokens (follow-up).
acceptance_criteria: WRAC implemented as a first-class admission module in the runtime admission pipeline (code merged on main)
Sliding-window reservoirs configurable at 30s/5m/1h with decay and per-tenant caps exposed via config
Admission decision outputs one of: ALLOW, PROB_EVICT (probabilistic drop), Fallback=SLIM_RESPONSE, Fallback=COARSE_MODEL, Fallback=CACHE_HIT, DROP. Generator must emit reason codes for metrics
End-to-end integration tests demonstrating predictable smoothing for synthetic burst patterns (unit+integration), test artifacts in CI
Canary rollout in eu-west-1 with 5% of traffic routed to WRAC; SLOs for latency and error rate not breached during 48h canary
Observability: dashboards show reservoir fill/decay, admit rate, fallback type distribution, per-tenant fairness score; alerts for >1% global DROP rate
Runbook updated with playbook for manual override and fallback policy changes
design_decisions: Use exponential decay on reservoir tokens instead of strict sliding-window recalculation to reduce memory churn and CPU overhead
Admission return codes must be deterministic based on request fingerprint + reservoir state when possible to avoid client confusion
Probabilistic eviction uses a stable reservoir-seed per tenant to avoid correlated drops across concurrent requests
Fallback preference order: CACHE_HIT -> SLIM_RESPONSE -> COARSE_MODEL -> DROP to maximize user-perceived value
Cross-region failover: reservoir state replicated asynchronously to neighbor regions; on hard failover we apply conservative halving of reservoirs to avoid burst amplification
No API surface change: policy tuning via internal Console controls (feature flag gated)
Telemetry: emit compact histograms for bucket fullness and sample traces for admitted+fallback flows
rollout_plan: 1) Merge feature-flag gated WRAC behind ff/wrac-default=false. 2) Unit and integration test pass, merge to canary branch. 3) Canary: enable in eu-west-1 at 5% traffic for 48h with close monitoring of latency and error SLOs. 4) If canary passes, increase to 25% for 24h and validate fairness metrics. 5) Global rollout in waves by region (NA -> EU -> APAC). 6) Enable cross-region reservoir share in a final step after per-region stability confirmed. 7) Post-rollout: 2-week observation window and retrospective.
runbook: If global_drop_rate fires: reduce WRAC-enabled traffic fraction to 0 and rollback feature flag; notify SRE oncall
If a single tenant shows sustained high DROP: apply manual override: set per-tenant cap to high value and initiate customer outreach
For cross-region failover anomalies: switch to region-local reservoir mode and pause async replication
Manual ops: ff/wrac-default=true enables global mode; ff/wrac-force-legacy disables WRAC at proxy ingress
